newsitem.title: USA: AT&T reports 14 percent gain in operating results.
newsitem.headline: AT&T reports 14 percent gain in operating results.

text.p: AT&T Corp. Wednesday reported a 14 percent gain in profits from continuing operations for the final quarter of 1996, when it completed a major restructuring of its businesses.
The telecommunications company said it earned $1.24 billion, or 76 cents a share, in the quarter, compared with operating profit of $1.09 billion, or 68 cents a share, in the same period of 1995.
Revenues in the latest period rose to $13.24 billion from $12.89 billion.

The New York-based company's 1995 fourth-quarter operating profits excluded restructuring and other charges totalling $2.036 billion, or $1.27 per share. Including these charges, its net earnings from continuing operations resulted in a loss of $948 million, or 59 cents a share.

For all of 1996, AT&T's income from continuing operations rose to $5.6 billion from $5.2 billion for 1995, excluding the charges. Earnings per share for 1996 were $3.47, a 5.5 percent increase over $3.29 per share in 1995.
Total 1996 revenues were $52.2 billion, a 3 percent increase over 1995's $50.7 billion in revenues.
"AT&T had a record year in 1996 in the face of extraordinary challenges and unprecedented changes in our business and in our industry," said Chairman Robert E. Allen.

"Income from continuing operations was a record $5.6 billion, up 7 percent from 1995. At the same time, we executed a value-creating trivestiture, spinning off Lucent (Technologies) and NCR to AT&T shareowners. Those companies today have a combined market value of $37 billion, far in excess of their value as part of the old AT&T."

In September of 1995, AT&T said it would restructure its businesses, a process completed with the spinoff of NCR at the end of 1996. AT&T prreviously concluded the spinoff of its majority holding in Lucent Technologies to AT&T shareowners and sold its majority position in AT&T Capital Corporation to a consortium of investors.

The company said its latest quarterly results were hit by higher uncollectibles in its communications services business, reflecting collection issues and a shift in industry-wide credit risk profiles of business customers, which led to increased fraud, delinquencies and bankruptcies. Those factors resulted in approximately $200 million in increased expenses.

AT&T said its communications services revenue increased $529 million in the latest quarter, up 4.3 percent from the same period last year. Communications services revenues include wireline services and wireless services, as well as communications products and other services.
It said its long distance calling volumes grew 6 percent over the same period in 1995 and 1.8 percent over the previous quarter.

AT&T's wireless services revenue, which includes cellular voice and data, messaging and air-to-ground services, grew 18.4 percent to $937 million in the fourth quarter of 1996. Its cellular service subscribers grew to 5.2 million, a 31.7 percent increase from a year ago.

Revenues from communications products and other services, which include consulting and outsourcing, on-line, and wireless product sales, were $386 million, an increase of nearly 17 percent from the year-ago quarter.

However, Financial Services revenue decreased 32.3 percent to $374 million, primarily as a result of the securitization programme instituted at AT&T Universal Card Services in 1995 to diversify funding sources as well as lower card use and promotional pricing. At year-end, Universal Card Services had $6.5 billion of securitized receivables, up from $3.5 billion at the end of 1995.
AT&T's stock slipped 62.5 cents to $38.75 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
